title: The AI app builder your team trusts has a root-level backdoor
excerpt: A critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-0768 (CVSS 9.8), in the open-source AI app-building platform Langflow is under active,...
content_html:
A critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-0768 (CVSS 9.8), in the open-source AI app-building platform Langflow is under active, ongoing exploitation since August 29, 2026. The flaw lives in Langflow's custom component validate endpoint, which passes user-submitted code directly into Python's exec() with no authentication or input validation in many default deployments, letting attackers run arbitrary code as root. Attackers then harvest .env files, SSH keys, OpenAI API keys, AWS credentials and database secrets, exfiltrate them, and attempt lateral movement. VulnCheck logged over 360 exploitation attempts on UK honeypots, mostly from Russia, and twelve Langflow vulnerabilities have been exploited in 2026 versus just one in all prior years combined, with over 15,000 successful exploits recorded across related CVEs. Recommended actions: patch immediately (all versions through 1.4.2 are affected), rotate every credential that touched an exposed instance regardless of confirmed exploitation, and never expose AI development platforms to the internet without authentication.

What is CVE-2026-0768 and how does it affect Langflow?

CVE-2026-0768 is a critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability (CVSS 9.8) in Langflow's custom component validate endpoint, which passes submitted code directly into Python's exec() without validation. In many default deployments no authentication is required, letting an attacker reaching the instance over the network execute arbitrary Python code as root with no credentials or user interaction. All Langflow versions up to and including 1.4.2 are affected. Teams running Langflow in production can track emerging vulnerability disclosures like this one on daily.dev.

What should I do if my Langflow instance was exposed to CVE-2026-0768?

Patch immediately and rotate every credential that touched the exposed instance, including OpenAI API keys, AWS credentials, SSH keys, and database secrets, even if exploitation was not confirmed. The attack chain specifically harvests .env files and environment variables, and stolen credentials remain useful until rotated regardless of whether the underlying vulnerability has since been patched. Developers responding to credential exposure incidents follow security advisories like this through daily.dev.

How many Langflow vulnerabilities have been exploited in the wild in 2026?

Twelve Langflow vulnerabilities have been exploited in 2026, compared to only one in all previous years combined. VulnCheck has recorded over 15,000 successful exploitation attempts across three related flaws (CVE-2026-0769, CVE-2025-3248, and CVE-2026-5027) prior to CVE-2026-0768, with over 360 exploitation attempts logged on UK honeypots alone, mostly originating from Russia. Security-conscious teams evaluating AI tooling risk track exploitation trends like these via daily.dev.
